claim: RAUC system.conf reference (latest docs): min-bundle-version rejects a bundle whose manifest version is older, but the docs warn that tying bundle version to system version conflicts with rollback ('1.2.9 = good; update to 1.3.0 with limit set to 1.3.0; problems!; update-bundle version:=1.3.1 but with content=1.2.9'); prevent-late-fallback runs the equivalent of 'rauc status mark-bad other' after mark-good so the older slot is no longer eligible for fallback; the D-Bus InstallBundle argument ignore-version-limit disables the check. Both options are off by default.

heise (38C3, Dec 2024): Thomas Lambertz's bitpixie attack downgrades the boot chain to an outdated Windows boot loader that Secure Boot still accepts, extracts the BitLocker key from RAM; considered fixed since Nov 2022 but still exploitable by downgrade because revoking the vulnerable loaders' certificates is limited by UEFI firmware revocation storage; needs one-time physical access and network boot.

The Hacker News (Aug 2024): SafeBreach's Windows Downdate (Black Hat USA 2024) abuses the OS's own update process to roll back DLLs and the NT kernel so a fully patched system becomes exposed to past vulnerabilities; CVE-2024-21302 (CVSS 6.7) and CVE-2024-38202; Microsoft's first mitigation was an opt-in revocation policy; most variants need admin rights.

Boles et al., 'Deciphering Discrepancies: A Comparative Analysis of Docker Image Security' (SCAM 2024 NIER, Montana State/INL/PNNL): 927 images scanned with Trivy and Grype; the tools agreed on the vulnerability count in only 15.3% of images (142/927), Grype reported more in 84.6%, and they disagreed 60,799 times on the severity of identical vulnerability IDs; discrepancies trace to partially overlapping, contradictory vulnerability databases.

Debian LTS list, Adrian Bunk (2025-04-26): 'no-dsa' and 'postponed' mean the CVE alone won't justify a DSA but 'it should be fixed in pu (or as part of a DSA for other CVEs)'; 'ignored' means 'there is a good reason why the CVE should never be fixed'; he also calls some '<ignored> (Minor issue)' tags wrong (tags applied inconsistently).

Buildroot LTS page: LTS support extended to 3 years starting with 2025.02 (previously 1 year); 'paid LTS stewards are assigned to the weekly LTS maintenance tasks', funded by sponsorship; vulnerability fixes on master are prioritised for backport; tracking at security.buildroot.org; no explicit end date and no default package coverage list stated; many of the 2,000+ packages have no upstream LTS.

raspberrypi/usbboot docs/secure-boot.md: the signed boot.img 'should contain' config.txt, 'Device tree and overlay files', GPU firmware, kernel and initramfs; once OTP is programmed 'it cannot be disabled and a different key cannot be programmed'; no anti-rollback or key revocation for signed boot images is described, and tryboot/A-B boot partitions are not covered.

Raspberry Pi security architecture page: secure boot stores a hash of the customer public key in device OTP; the EEPROM bootloader verifies boot.img's signature (boot.sig) and on BCM2712 (Pi 5) the customer key also signs the EEPROM bootloader; on failure it 'doesn't continue with the untrusted software'; the page does not cover anti-rollback, revocation, or the unsigned (default) case.
